eligibility.evidence: Abstract and Sec. 2 (pp. 1-3): LLMs run as agents on stochastic Bernoulli multi-armed bandits, framed as an RL exploration problem and compared with UCB/Thompson sampling baselines. The paradigm is cited to bandit theory (Slivkins; Lattimore and Szepesvari), not to a human cognitive study. Human bandit work appears only in related work (Sec. 4, p. 14) as other papers' designs. E2 operational test fails; borderline because bandit tasks overlap with learning and decision-making paradigms.

A.title: Can Large Language Models Explore In-Context?
A.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024)

G.notes: Excluded at full text on E2: bandit exploration is treated as an RL capability with algorithmic baselines and no human comparison. A referee may argue bandits are a learning/decision paradigm (borderline). Sections beyond Sec. 2 start not coded because decision is NO.
